summary: Gifford Pinchot NF site of a 1930s patrol point and emergency fire lookout above the Lewis River canyon; now gone, reached by Forest Service trail 30A.

facts.design: Shed structure, per a recently found image (Willhite)
facts.status_note: Lookout gone. Sources describe a fire finder base and tie-down anchors at the site, and do not say whether any of the shed remains.
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Gifford Pinchot National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot by Forest Service Trail 30A from the Spencer Butte Trail.

visit.trail_note: Trail 30A leaves the Spencer Butte Trail. The Forest Service gives 1.2 miles to the site; Willhite gives 0.8 miles from a junction 0.3 miles from the summit. Willhite's directions take paved FR 93, about 7.6 miles from FR 25, to a high saddle with parking.

events.note: Register and firelookout.com give only 'the 1930s'; 1930 marks the start of that decade, not a dated record

evidence.supports: built in the 1930s; now gone
evidence.quote: Built in the 1930s, this lookout is now gone.

evidence.supports: registered June 23, 2012 as US 1308, WA 208
build date unknown to firelookout.com; site gone
evidence.quote: 1930s: unknown. Gone.

evidence.quote: Gifford Pinchot National Forest

notes_for_editor: Two source conflicts left open, both shown in the story: trail length (Forest Service 1.2 miles; Willhite 0.8 miles from the junction, attributed to a Gifford Pinchot guide) and whether the fire finder base remains (Forest Service says it can still be seen; Willhite's quote of the guide adds 'since removed'). Willhite calls it a patrol point with an emergency-lookout role; the record kind 'unknown' was left as is. No build year is given beyond the 1930s. No new photos. Willhite's 2019 photo captions give no date for the cable anchors.
